Gene-wise posterior + test statistic + p-value without storing posterior matrices

Source: R/compute_test_per_gene.R
compute_test_per_gene.Rd

This function reproduces the behavior of compute_posterior(), compute_test_statistic(), and compute_pvalue(), but it computes everything one gene at a time without ever allocating an n x p posterior mean/variance matrix. It refuses the same settings as compute_posterior, among them bool_adjust_covariates = TRUE together with bool_covariates_as_library = TRUE.

Usage

compute_test_per_gene(
  input_obj,
  alpha_max = 1000,
  bool_adjust_covariates = FALSE,
  bool_covariates_as_library = TRUE,
  bool_stabilize_underdispersion = TRUE,
  library_min = 0.1,
  min_cells_per_individual = 3,
  nuisance_lower_quantile = 0.01,
  pseudocount = 0,
  verbose = 0
)

Arguments

input_obj

eSVD object after nuisance estimation.

alpha_max

Upper bound on the fitted mean without the library, before it forms the prior (same role as in compute_posterior.eSVD); default 1e3.

bool_adjust_covariates

Boolean; if TRUE, divide the posterior numerator (count plus prior) by the exponentiated effect of the confounding covariates (same as in compute_posterior.default).

bool_covariates_as_library

Boolean; if TRUE, include non–case-control covariates in the covariate-adjusted library size.

bool_stabilize_underdispersion

Boolean; if TRUE, mean-center log10(nuisance_vec) when its mean is above 0, i.e. when the geometric mean of the rates is above 1 (less over-dispersion than a unit rate; see compute_posterior.eSVD).

library_min

Minimum value for the covariate-adjusted library size; default 0.1, the same as compute_posterior.eSVD.

min_cells_per_individual

Minimum number of cells an individual must contribute; see compute_test_statistic.

nuisance_lower_quantile

Lower quantile at which to floor nuisance_vec, one number in [0, 1]; NULL means no floor.

pseudocount

Numeric; additional count added to each entry in the count matrix when forming the posterior.

verbose

Integer; controls printed messages.

Value

The input eSVD object with:

  • teststat_vec — Welch t-statistics (length p).

  • case_mean — case Gaussian means per gene.

  • control_mean — control Gaussian means per gene.

  • case_var, control_var — the variance of each arm, the two quantities the statistic divides by.

  • log2fc_vec, log2fc_se_vec — the log2 fold change and its standard error; see compute_log_fold_change.

  • pvalue_list — list with df_vec, fdr_vec, gaussian_teststat, log10pvalue, method, null_mean, null_sd; see compute_pvalue.

The individuals of each arm are recorded in param, as compute_test_statistic does, and so are the settings of the posterior, under the names compute_posterior uses (posterior_alpha_max and so on). Calling the function again overwrites them.

Examples

set.seed(10)
sim <- generate_null(cell_per_person = 15, num_genes = 40,
                     num_individuals = 8)
esvd_obj <- initialize_esvd(dat = sim$obs_mat,
                            covariates = sim$covariates,
                            metadata_individual = sim$metadata_individual,
                            case_control_variable = "CC",
                            bool_intercept = TRUE,
                            k = 2,
                            lambda = 0.1)
esvd_obj <- reparameterization_esvd_covariates(input_obj = esvd_obj,
                                               fit_name = "fit_Init",
                                               omitted_variables = "Log_UMI")
esvd_obj <- opt_esvd(input_obj = esvd_obj,
                     max_iter = 5,
                     offset_variables = setdiff(colnames(esvd_obj$covariates), "CC"),
                     fit_name = "fit_First",
                     fit_previous = "fit_Init")
esvd_obj <- reparameterization_esvd_covariates(input_obj = esvd_obj,
                                               fit_name = "fit_First",
                                               omitted_variables = "Log_UMI")
esvd_obj <- estimate_nuisance(input_obj = esvd_obj)
esvd_obj <- compute_test_per_gene(input_obj = esvd_obj,
                                  alpha_max = 2 * max(sim$obs_mat))
utils::head(esvd_obj$teststat_vec)
#>    gene_1    gene_2    gene_3    gene_4    gene_5    gene_6 
#> -4.710563 -4.069603  1.434486  4.243108 -2.545816  5.770229 
# no cell-by-gene posterior matrices were stored
names(esvd_obj$fit_First)
#>  [1] "x_mat"                       "y_mat"                      
#>  [3] "z_mat"                       "loss"                       
#>  [5] "nuisance_vec"                "nuisance_mle_vec"           
#>  [7] "nuisance_library_median_vec" "nuisance_status"            
#>  [9] "gene_mean_count_vec"         "gene_sparsity_vec"
